summary: @nebula.js/sn-listbox preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's `preinstall` lifecycle script (`node setup.mjs`) runs automatically on `npm install`. `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (hex-mangled identifiers, per-scope string-property dictionaries hiding literals such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `Alpine`, `bun`, `powershell`, `Expand-Archive`), performs platform/libc detection, downloads the Bun runtime archive from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<platform>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, sets it executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunBinary, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. The invoked file `math_init.js` is a 727 KB bundle carrying the `@bun`/`@bun-cjs` header and obfuscator.io-style artifacts (string-array rotator function, multi-thousand-entry constants array, hex-mangled identifiers). Executing bundled code under a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime rather than Node evades Node-based supply-chain scanners; the payload's network and filesystem behavior are opaque. A Qlik listbox UI supernova has no legitimate need to fetch Bun and run an obfuscated bundle at install time, and this behavior does not appear in the legitimate `@nebula.js/sn-listbox` releases. This is an alternate-runtime dropper executing attacker-controlled bytes on the installer's host at `npm install` time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
